# Implementation Summary (Issue #511)

## What we learned

- Import-rejection Handoff expires the current claim; a plain issue-work rerun acquires a new claim, so strictly claim-bound context cannot automatically survive that path.

## Working Tree Changes
```text
 M internal/lease/manager.go
 M internal/lease/manager_test.go
 M internal/lease/plan_replan.go
 M internal/workflow/claim_budget_test.go
 M internal/workflow/engine.go
 M internal/workflow/execute_implementation.go
 M internal/workflow/execute_plan.go
 M internal/workflow/execute_run.go
 M internal/workflow/execute_validation.go
 M internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go
?? changes/unreleased/511.md
```

## Diff Stat
```text
AGENTS.md                                   | 17 ++++++++
 internal/lease/manager.go                   | 57 +++++++++++++++++++++++-
 internal/lease/manager_test.go              | 67 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 internal/lease/plan_replan.go               |  1 +

 internal/workflow/engine.go                 |  2 +-

 11 files changed, 296 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)
```

## Developer report

Status: PARTIAL

Implementation stopped for planning review after a failed lifecycle assumption. This candidate is not ready for tester validation or publication.

The plan assumes that a rejected import can retain the same claim for a plain ExecuteWork rerun while leaving Handoff unchanged. In fact, Manager.Handoff sets Lease.Status to "handoff" and ExpiresAt to now (internal/lease/manager.go, Handoff). Acquire then creates a new claim. The new TestPreviousAttemptImportRejection exercises this exact path: the second developer invocation receives no diagnostic because the saved diagnostic belongs to the previous claim. Suppression is required by the approved plan's instruction that diagnostics cannot cross claim boundaries. Resume is not a solution for an expired handoff claim.

AC1 is unmet. Resolving it needs an explicit plan decision on preserving the claim on rejection versus securely transferring diagnostic context at a successor claim. Neither change is part of the approved implementation sequence, which explicitly preserves handoff behavior and excludes cross-claim notes. No lifecycle bypass was added.

## Implemented reversible slice

- Optional structured per-role diagnostics in IssueState; fenced direct-issue recording checks expected task digest and claim inside CAS.
- Diagnostic clearing on artifact acceptance and changed-task approval; also covered the separate atomic planner-pair commit in plan_replan.go, discovered while tracing artifact writes.
- Runner wrapper refreshes state before prompt use, checks the claim, quotes refused paths, and measures only actual runner execution. It records typed timeouts/deadlines using a bounded uncancelled cleanup context and excludes budget pauses.
- Wrapped planner/developer/tester requests and the ordinary direct-issue reviewer request. Existing PR/fork paths and checkpoint-plan requests bypass the wrapper.
- Import-rejection recording preserves the existing Handoff and recovery wording; the regression demonstrates why this is insufficient under current claim semantics.
- Added a change fragment for the timeout slice. Import policy, harnesses, protected paths, retries and recovery imports were not changed.

## Review findings

F2: TestPreviousAttemptTimeout uses a zero-value sandbox.AgentTimeoutError and checks errors.As without formatting its Error() text.
F3: Timeout assertion checks the duration phrase, without assuming a wall-clock value.
F4: Reviewer sites traced: runAgentReview is ordinary direct-issue/PR review and also serves checkpoint review; wrapper explicitly excludes recovery.CandidateHead. execute_plan.go's separate runner.Run is checkpoint-plan drafting and stays unchanged. engine.go's other agent.RunReview is upstream candidate review and stays unchanged.

## Evidence and limitations

- Initial compile probe: `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease ./internal/workflow -run '^TestAttemptDiagnostic' -count=1` exited 0; package output 0.006s each, no matching tests at that point. This is compile evidence only for that intermediate source.
- `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^TestPreviousAttempt' -count=1` exited 1, 0.662s package time. Timeout wrapper cases passed; import-rejection case failed with all four expected diagnostic strings absent on the second invocation. This exposed the failed plan assumption. The timeout cases invoke the shared wrapper with all four role names; they do not yet independently prove each real request site through ExecuteWork.
- `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run '^TestAttemptDiagnostic' -count=1` exited 1, 0.040s package time: the accepted-artifact fixture lacked required producer and summary fields. Those fields were added afterward; no rerun was performed after the planning stop. This result cannot establish lifecycle success for final sources.
- gofmt ran on edited Go sources (exit 0). A broad workflow test-file glob was also formatted; no intended unrelated test changes.
- Source inspection used cat, grep and sed after discovering rg is unavailable; Python performed edits. sha256sum recorded final source identity. These diagnostics exited 0 except the initial combined read/search command, whose rg invocation exited 127.
- Unchanged-behavior baseline regression evidence was not obtained before implementation. Existing-guidance regression command, vet and staticcheck were not run: the role contract requires stopping for planning review on a failed assumption before further validation. No full suite or live model was run.
- AC2 and AC3 remain unverified for final sources. Persistence across fresh engines/managers, stale/expired/successor writers, hostile path/sentinel cases, generic cancellation, and PR/fork exclusion still need the full planned coverage after lifecycle scope review.

## Source identity

The task snapshot has no Git metadata. Coordinator must supply authoritative candidate identity. SHA-256 of the ordered `sha256sum` output for the changed files listed below (including changes/unreleased/511.md) is `eec43ef9338a3c309cd97cd9adde151302d700cfc16313e6cd0de7395a45b65f`.

## HANDOFF

Planning review is required before tester work. Do not treat intermediate results as final validation.

Changed files, in source-identity order:

1. internal/lease/manager.go
2. internal/lease/plan_replan.go
3. internal/lease/manager_test.go
4. internal/workflow/execute_run.go
5. internal/workflow/execute_plan.go
6. internal/workflow/execute_implementation.go
7. internal/workflow/execute_validation.go
8. internal/workflow/engine.go
9. internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go
10. internal/workflow/claim_budget_test.go
11. changes/unreleased/511.md

Behavior and observed command results are recorded above. AC1 fails reproducibly because Handoff ends the originating claim. AC2 has passing wrapper-only intermediate evidence; actual role-path regression coverage is incomplete. AC3 has incomplete fixture evidence and no passing final check. No acceptance criterion is claimed complete. The new failing import regression is retained for the planning decision; do not weaken it to hide the lifecycle conflict.

# ISSUE-511 plan

Carry coordinator-written rejection and timeout diagnostics into the next direct-issue invocation of the same role. This revision resolves the prior handoff conflict by transferring eligible diagnostics to the successor claim inside acquisition, rather than retaining an expired claim. The operator explicitly authorizes this same-task transfer; each usable note remains bound to the current claim. Dimensions remain small / known / standard, compact profile. Estimated remaining implementation and focused verification: 3–5 hours, within the 16-hour total claim budget.

## What we know

- The partial implementation is present: structured diagnostics, fenced recording and role-based artifact clearing exist in `internal/lease/manager.go:257–303`; prompt injection and timeout measurement exist in `internal/workflow/execute_run.go:350` onward.
- `Handoff` changes status to handoff and expires the lease (`internal/lease/manager.go:1673`). `acquire` generates a new ID and replaces the lease before its CAS save (`internal/lease/manager.go:1176`). It currently does not rebind diagnostics. The prompt wrapper requires the diagnostic claim to equal the current claim. This explains the failure without relying on the previous report.
- `TestPreviousAttemptImportRejection` already exercises a real manual ExecuteWork rerun after rejection (`internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go:676`); retain its assertions. `TestPreviousAttemptTimeout` currently exercises only the wrapper (`internal/workflow/claim_budget_test.go:806`), so actual role-site coverage is still needed.
- Actual coordinator request sites wrap planner/developer/tester runs (`execute_plan.go:92`, `execute_implementation.go:134`, `execute_validation.go:61`) and ordinary direct-issue review (`engine.go:1188`), all under `internal/workflow/`. Checkpoint planning (`execute_plan.go:357`) and upstream review (`engine.go:1938`) bypass this wrapper.
- Artifact clearing has multiple call sites in `internal/lease/manager.go:1932`, `:2270`, `:2348`, `:3705`, plus the atomic planner pair in `internal/lease/plan_replan.go:382`. Changed-task approval clears diagnostics (`manager.go:1079`).
- `.swarm/config.yaml` selects isolated native Codex on Linux and Claude for review. Native adapter admission is capability-qualified (`internal/agent/configured.go:84`); the coordinator request sites above support injected runners independently of live harness admission. Real Claude/native qualification is not established by these unit tests and is not a prerequisite for the coordinator fix.
- Budget interruption is a distinct cause (`internal/workflow/claim_budget.go:94`); pause paths can hand off (`:144`). A generic cancellation or budget admission refusal is not an agent timeout.

## What we're assuming

- The current partial slice can be completed without changing the state schema or harnesses; check JSON compatibility and tests before integrating. Earlier intermediate passing results are not final evidence.
- Diagnostics are advisory context, so carrying them between owners for the same task is appropriate. This is explicitly authorized by the operator; it transfers no approval, artifact, reservation, or mutation rights.

## Open questions

- Exact accepted-artifact clearing coverage is resolved by step 3's source audit and lifecycle tests, including planner-pair commits and failed writes.
- The snapshot has no authoritative Git base identity available from the previous run. The coordinator must supply base/candidate identity. All proposed source files already exist in this snapshot; no new files, deletions or renames are planned, so no new-file base absence claim is needed.
- Live OCI/Bubblewrap, other OSes, and real model execution are outside this coordinator-only change. Verify request composition using injected runners on Linux, including the reviewer helper; do not modify harness policy to make live tests available.

## Decision and exact changes

Preserve Handoff, acquisition admission, expiry, approval, retry accounting, recovery patches and NextPhaseReason semantics. Modify `internal/lease/manager.go` acquisition so transfer occurs in the same CAS save as the successor lease. Capture predecessor claim ID, task digest and direct-issue eligibility before lease replacement or fork cleanup. After approved-base preparation, retain only coordinator diagnostic entries with allowed roles/kinds, predecessor claim binding and unchanged task digest, and only when both predecessor and successor are direct issues. Rebind their ClaimID to the new claim ID. Discard mismatched entries. Require nonempty predecessor binding. Never infer transfer eligibility from comments, NextPhaseReason, artifacts, agent files, owner equality, or arbitrary error strings. A task change discards the note even if an old record survives serialization.

Transfer applies to eligible latest per-role notes after handoff and to eligible notes when an expired/stopped claim is replaced, covering timeout stops as well as import rejection. A still-active claim uses existing resume semantics. A changed owner is permitted by ordinary acquisition authorization. Old writers retain their old token and fail with wrapped ErrClaimFence. CAS failure must neither bind the manager to the new claim nor commit a transfer. Repeated successor claims may carry an uncleared note; its lifetime ends at same-role artifact acceptance or changed task, not at a successful process return. PR/fork acquisition must not carry or later revive direct-issue diagnostics.

Modify existing files only:

- `internal/lease/manager.go`: atomic acquisition transfer helper/integration, structured validation as necessary, existing recording and clearing paths.
- `internal/lease/plan_replan.go`: preserve or correct atomic planner-pair clearing if the lifecycle audit finds a gap.
- `internal/workflow/execute_run.go`: retain refresh, strict current claim/task checks, quoting and fixed report instruction; complete classified timeout handling and error propagation if required by tests. Record only actual invocation timeout/deadline, measured with monotonic elapsed time, with bounded uncancelled cleanup and the original claim fence. Never label generic cancellation, budget pause or admission/setup errors as timeout.
- `internal/workflow/execute_plan.go`, `execute_implementation.go`, `execute_validation.go`, `engine.go`: retain the existing final request wrappers and operator/revision text; adjust only if actual role-path tests reveal missing direct-issue composition.
- `internal/workflow/import_guidance_test.go`, `claim_budget_test.go`; `internal/lease/manager_test.go`, `claim_fence_test.go`: extend regression and lifecycle coverage.
- `changes/unreleased/511.md`: modify the existing fragment to describe rejection and timeout context through successor claims.

## Implementation sequence

1. Retain the failing import regression and capture its pre-fix failure on this snapshot. Add focused lease tests for same-task handoff/expiry transfer, changed-task suppression and stale writers. Implement transfer within acquisition's existing CAS transaction. Result: successor state has matching task/current-claim notes; old writer cannot mutate it, including same-owner successors.
2. Exercise timeout through each real planner/developer/tester/reviewer coordinator request site. Persist before existing error/stop handling; manually resume or reacquire according to that path. Keep automatic retry/settlement behavior unchanged. Use fresh Engine/Manager instances to prove durable handoff transfer. Result: next same-role prompt has fixed timeout text and elapsed duration, without model calls or long sleeps.
3. Verify all acceptance/clearing paths, JSON compatibility, other-role isolation, changed-task reapproval, failed artifact writes, and PR/fork exclusion. Ensure transfer cannot resurrect an entry already cleared by an accepted artifact. Result: only current task/current claim coordinator diagnostics enter prompts; refused output remains unimported.
4. Run focused checks in TEST_PLAN.md, preserve existing refusal/recovery wording, and update the existing changelog fragment. Record source identity and results in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Result: all three acceptance criteria have applicable evidence.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved inputs or gates.

- Entry points: `Manager.acquire` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1176`), `Handoff` (`:1673`), `RecordAttemptDiagnostic` (`:266`), `clearAttemptDiagnostic` (`:291`), changed-task clearing (`:1079`); `RecordPlanPair` (`internal/lease/plan_replan.go:382`); `rejectImport` (`internal/workflow/execute_run.go:150`), `attemptRunner.Run` (same file, search symbol); request sites listed above.
- Extend existing `TestPreviousAttemptImportRejection`, `TestPreviousAttemptTimeout`, `TestAttemptDiagnosticLifecycle`, `budgetEngine` and `budgetTestRunner`. Use `TestPreviousAttempt*` / `TestAttemptDiagnostic*` prefixes for added cases.
- Exact focused commands: `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^TestPreviousAttempt' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run '^TestAttemptDiagnostic' -count=1`; `go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(CompletedUnownedActiveOutputGuidance|UnownedActiveGuidanceFallback|DeveloperOutputRejectionGuidance|ImportRejectionReasonRouting|BudgetPauseStillRequiresFence)$' -count=1`; `go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease`.
- Checked assumptions: read acquisition, handoff, timeout wrapper, actual request sites and existing regression source. The reported claim conflict is confirmed. No planner test execution or implementation changes are claimed.
- Reopen for harness/protected-policy changes, fork gateway operations, automatic retries, recovery import, or broader lease lifecycle changes. The authorized diagnostic transfer itself is now explicitly in scope.
- **What this change breaks:** search results identify strict claim filtering in `attemptRunner.Run` (preserve, rebind at acquisition instead); old plan language forbidding all cross-claim notes (superseded by this operator-authorized atomic transfer); existing import regression (make pass without weakening); wrapper-only timeout tests (retain and add real-site coverage); state lifecycle fixtures in manager tests (extend for transfer). Exact rejection/CLI recovery text in `import_guidance_test.go` and NextPhaseReason consumers stays unchanged. PR/fork routing, checkpoint-plan/upstream reviewer calls, retry settlement, repair/revision prompts, import policy and recovery-patch tests remain unchanged. Existing changelog fragment is modified; docs/templates/adapters need no change. No files are removed or renamed.

## Operator guidance

> Resolve the handoff/claim-boundary conflict: when an import rejection or timeout occurs, either preserve the active claim across that stop or carry the coordinator-written rejection/timeout diagnostic across the handoff to the successor claim for the same task digest (still dropping it once the role records an accepted artifact).

# ISSUE-511 test plan

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete tests and evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1: refusal context; initial prompt clean | Retain `TestPreviousAttemptImportRejection`: actual developer CheckImport refusal of `.swarm/active/DEV_NOTES.md`, then manual ExecuteWork rerun. Assert handoff expires the old claim, successor ID differs, note is rebound, actual next TaskPrompt includes refused path and IMPLEMENTATION.md instruction, first prompt has no section, private output is absent, rejected file remains absent. Add fresh Engine/Manager successor variant. |
| 2: timeout and elapsed time | Extend `TestPreviousAttemptTimeout*` beyond wrapper tests: invoke real planner/developer/tester/reviewer coordinator paths using injected runners and existing budget fixtures. Return typed timeout or actual run deadline, manually resume or reacquire after stop, capture next same-role TaskPrompt and assert timeout text and elapsed duration. Cover a handoff and an expired successor claim. Use deterministic short deadlines/clock control and broad bounds; no long sleeps. Other roles, setup/admission failures, generic cancellation and budget-only pause receive no timeout note. |
| 3: accepted artifact and changed task | `TestPreviousAttemptLifecycle*` and `TestAttemptDiagnostic*`: accepted artifact clears only its role atomically; another role's artifact and successful runner alone do not clear; failed artifact persistence does not clear. Cover planner pair, review, implementation and validation. Reapprove changed WorkUnit digest and reacquire: no section. Further successor acquisition cannot resurrect cleared entries. |
| Constraints and operator transfer | Lease tests cover JSON absent-field compatibility/round-trip, latest same-role replacement, same-task handoff and expired claim transfer, different owner and same owner successors, repeated transfer, task mismatch, invalid predecessor claim, stale/expired writer and CAS race rejection. Assert failed CAS leaves stored binding and manager token unchanged. PR/fork predecessor or successor cannot carry/revive notes. Workflow tests keep strict current claim/task filtering, escaped hostile refused paths, fixed coordinator wording, and exclude agent output, arbitrary errors, operator text and private patch paths from the diagnostic. |

## Developer-owned focused checks

First record the retained import regression failure before the transfer fix; then run the following after implementation. Prior intermediate evidence in WORKUNIT.md does not establish correctness of this candidate.

```bash
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^TestPreviousAttempt' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/lease -run '^TestAttemptDiagnostic' -count=1
go test -timeout=5m ./internal/workflow -run '^Test(CompletedUnownedActiveOutputGuidance|UnownedActiveGuidanceFallback|DeveloperOutputRejectionGuidance|ImportRejectionReasonRouting|BudgetPauseStillRequiresFence)$' -count=1
go vet ./internal/workflow ./internal/lease
```

Run gofmt on modified Go files. Expected duration per command: under five minutes. Record command, duration, exit status, relevant output, candidate commit and dirty-diff digest (or coordinator-provided identity plus changed-file hashes when Git metadata is unavailable) in `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Tests run on Linux with injected runners; no external network, container, live harness or paid model call is needed. Do not expose private timeout constructors solely for tests; existing typed fixtures must preserve error classification without formatting an invalid zero-value error.

## Tester-owned independent review

Independently inspect final source and map all three criteria to evidence. Verify acquisition eligibility uses predecessor state before replacement/fork cleanup, rebinding occurs in the same CAS save, digest matching survives base preparation, stale writers remain fenced, and no approval or retry state transfers with a note. Review all artifact acceptance paths, actual reviewer invocation and timeout cleanup. Verify actual successor prompt capture, not merely formatter tests; import policy and no-import assertions must remain intact.

Reuse passing developer results applicable to the same source identity. Record acceptance findings, evidence identity and applicability in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`. Repeat only checks affected by relevant source changes, observed failures or a concrete unresolved coverage concern. Agent observations are advisory and cannot satisfy claim-bound validation or publication.

## Coordinator-owned reference policy

The coordinator runs the complete trusted-base required policy once on the final candidate after roles finish; SYSTEM_PROMPT.md holds the reference. It is not a developer/tester execution checklist. Potential checks exceeding five minutes have exactly one owner below; publication reuses applicable coordinator results bound to final candidate and policy.

| Command/check | Owner | Expected duration | Evidence and reuse |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `go test -timeout=10m ./internal/validation/... ./internal/harness/... ./internal/coordination/... ./internal/lease/... ./internal/contract/...` | coordinator | 5–15 minutes | Coordinator validation record with final candidate/policy identity; publication reuses. |
| `go test -timeout=20m -parallel=8 ./internal/cli -run '^Test[A-M]'` | coordinator | 5–20 minutes | Same coordinator record and binding; no agent rerun. |
| `go test -timeout=20m -parallel=8 ./internal/cli -run '^Test([^A-M]|$)'` | coordinator | 5–20 minutes | Same coordinator record and binding; no agent rerun. |

Other required checks are expected under five minutes each. No additional long role checks are planned. If a focused check unexpectedly exceeds five minutes, developer remains its sole owner, records actual duration/evidence/source identity, and tester reuses it unless applicability changes.
